react_result.final_narrative_text: The differentially abundant metabolites converge overwhelmingly on arachidonic acid metabolism as the dominant biological signal. Three independent paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-direct activity) all rank Arachidonic acid metabolism / Eicosanoid synthesis as the top hit with FDR p=6.84e-14 (RaMP) and p=0.001 (Mummichog). The driver set comprises five eicosanoid derivatives — 5-HETE, 15-HETE, leukotriene A4, 15-deoxy-delta-12,14-PGJ2, and arachidonic acid itself — all confirmed as ChEBI canonical members with consistent first-block InChIKeys (KGIJOOYOSFUGPC, JSFATNQSLKRBCI, UFPQIRYSPUYQHK, VHRUMKCAEVRUBK, YZXBAPSDXZZRGB) across all tools. Arachidonic acid (KEGG:C00219) is the pathway substrate; 5-HETE and 15-HETE are lipoxygenase products (ALOX5/ALOX15); leukotriene A4 is the 5-lipoxygenase branch product; 15-deoxy-PGJ2 is a cyclopentenone prostaglandin formed via COX/non-enzymatic oxidation. Glycolaldehyde and losartan did not appear in any enriched pathway, indicating they are likely assay background or pharmacologically exogenous. The biological interpretation is that the treatment shifts arachidonic acid flux through both the lipoxygenase (HETE, leukotriene) and COX/cyclopentenone branches, consistent with inflammatory or eicosanoid-signalling modulation.

react_result.final_narrative_text: The seven differentially abundant metabolites resolve to two distinct biological signals. Five of them (5-HETE, 15-HETE, leukotriene A4, 15-deoxy-delta-12,14-PGJ2, and arachidonic acid) are canonical eicosanoid derivatives of the arachidonic acid cascade and they converge on a single dominant pathway in both RaMP ORA and Mummichog m/z-direct analysis. In RaMP, Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) achieves rank 0 with FDR 6.84e-14, fold enrichment 1430, and five of the input metabolites present as hits (5-HETE, 15-HETE, leukotriene A4, 15-deoxy-delta-12,14-PGJ2, arachidonic acid). In Mummichog, Arachidonic acid metabolism (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism) is ranked first with p=0.000588, capturing all five eicosanoid derivatives plus additional hydroxy and epoxy intermediates; Leukotriene metabolism (MUMM:leukotriene_metabolism) ranks fourth with p=0.037, capturing arachidonic acid and leukotriene A4. The two remaining metabolites, glycolaldehyde and losartan, do not map to the eicosanoid cluster and appear only in lower-scoring Mummichog entries (glycolaldehyde hits Glycerophospholipid metabolism, Glycolysis and Gluconeogenesis, Pyruvate Metabolism) with no RaMP enrichment. The driver set comprises the five eicosanoid derivatives, each confirmed as a ChEBI canonical member of WP:WP167 and as a hit in both RaMP and Mummichog outputs. Literature (PMID 41009650, 41439954) confirms that these metabolites are inflammatory derivatives of arachidonic acid and that their coordinated dysregulation reflects modulation of the eicosanoid synthesis pathway.

Three independent paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-direct activity) all rank Arachidonic acid metabolism / Eicosanoid synthesis as the top hit with FDR p=6.84e-14 (RaMP) and p=0.001 (Mummichog). The driver set comprises five eicosanoid derivatives — 5-HETE, 15-HETE, leukotriene A4, 15-deoxy-delta-12,14-PGJ2, and arachidonic acid itself — all confirmed as ChEBI canonical members with consistent first-block InChIKeys (KGIJOOYOSFUGPC, JSFATNQSLKRBCI, UFPQIRYSPUYQHK, VHRUMKCAEVRUBK, YZXBAPSDXZZRGB) across all tools.
